detalhes: Fonte: EC-OECD STIP Compass (Comissão Europeia e OCDE), edição 2025 da pesquisa STIP (dados atualizados até setembro de 2026); iniciativa 99997848, informada pelo governo do Brasil; última atualização no STIP: 25/08/2023. Iniciativa: Biodiversity Research Programme (Programa de Pesquisa em Biodiversidade) [PPBio]. País: Brasil. Período: desde 2004, sem data de término informada. Relação com o tema: política de formação e carreira em CTI que não menciona mulheres nem gênero (temas: Estratégias de recursos humanos em CTI). A descrição não fala de mulheres nem de gênero. Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI; Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): PPBio is a strategic programme at the national level to expand knowledge about the immense Brazilian biodiversity, filling knowledge gaps, especially in regions with difficult access and, therefore, with historical deficits in terms of scientific knowledge. Objetivos: 1) 1) efficiently apply already tested methodologies for monitoring biodiversity and ecosystem services. 2) 2) train and integrate local people responsible for monitoring biodiversity to maximize the quality and availability of information for decision-making on the degradation of environmental services associated with biodiversity, with the aim of minimizing environmental degradation, leading to the sustainable use of resources in natural and anthropized environments, such as agrosilvopastoral and urban, and still maximize the economic return and local and regional well-being. 3) 3) generate models and scenarios for the sustainable use of natural resources in the Brazilian territory and for the different biomes. 4) 4) modeling the impacts arising from extreme weather events and their impacts on biodiversity and ecosystem services, such as fire. Público-alvo: Pesquisadores estabelecidos; Estudantes de graduação e mestrado; Doutorandos; Institutos públicos de pesquisa. Temas no STIP: Estratégias de recursos humanos em CTI. Instrumentos: Financiamento institucional da pesquisa pública (Public Call); orçamento anual informado: de 1 a 5 milhões (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: o governo informa que a iniciativa foi avaliada. Contexto: Expand the formation of new research networks to cover all Brazilian biomes.

Relação com o tema: política de formação e carreira em CTI que não menciona mulheres nem gênero (temas: Mobilidade internacional de recursos humanos). A descrição não fala de mulheres nem de gênero. Responsável: National Council for Humanities, Science and Technology (CONAHCYT; Consejo Nacional de Humanidades, Ciencias y Tecnologías). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The program promotes the intensification and consolidation of the scientific and technological collaboration of Mexico with various countries of the world. Objetivos: 1) Link, disseminate, promote bilateral cooperation programs, signed with homologous institutions abroad, for the benefit of the national scientific and technological community. Público-alvo: Pesquisadores estabelecidos; Pós-doutorandos e pesquisadores em início de carreira; Instituições de ensino superior. Temas no STIP: Internacionalização da pesquisa pública; Mobilidade internacional de recursos humanos; Governança internacional de CTI. Contexto: CONACYT has carried out an intense activity in order to take advantage from international opportunities to improve the quality of Mexican universities, PRIs and their programmes and projects. This included establishing a number or multilateral and bilateral international agreements. The goal of international co-operation agreements is to create linkages, and to spread and promote the participation of Mexican experts in the activities of multilateral programmes and organisations. These agreements cover a wide range of S&T cooperation areas, including the international mobility of human resources.

tipo: Política ou iniciativa de CTI (OECD STIP Compass)

detalhes: Fonte: EC-OECD STIP Compass (Comissão Europeia e OCDE), edição 2023 da pesquisa STIP (dados atualizados até dezembro de 2024); iniciativa 24029, informada pelo governo do Chile; última atualização no STIP: 29/06/2023. Iniciativa: Be Part of Innovation (Súmate a innovar). País: Chile. Período: desde 2014, sem data de término informada. Relação com o tema: política de CTI que inclui mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade entre seus objetivos ou públicos (o governo marcou Mulheres entre os grupos-alvo; um instrumento promove a igualdade de gênero). Atenção: esta iniciativa aparece só na edição 2023 do STIP Compass; o governo não a informou de novo em 2025, e ela pode ter sido encerrada ou substituída. Responsável: Productive Development Corporation (CORFO; Corporación de Fomento de la Producción). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): This instrument seeks to improve the development of innovative solutions to problems and challenges in productivity and competitiveness of national enterprises through linkages with collaborative entities. Objetivos: 1) Improve the development of innovative solutions to problems and challenges in productivity and competitiveness of national enterprises. 2) Support the development of innovative solutions of firms that have never innovated before. 3) Encourage the development of new or improved products, services or processes that generate value to the company. 4) Promote the development of collaborative projects. Público-alvo: Mulheres; Sociedade civil; Empreendedores; Empresas de qualquer idade; Empresas de qualquer porte. Temas no STIP: Apoio financeiro a P&D e inovação nas empresas; Estímulo à demanda por inovação e criação de mercados. Instrumentos: Subvenção a P&D e inovação nas empresas; orçamento anual informado: de 1 a 5 milhões (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: o governo informa que a iniciativa foi avaliada. Contexto: Chile has similar levels of innovation to developed countries; however, it still shows large gaps in relation to its added value, generating US$0.4 per unit of material used, versus the OECD average of US$2.3.. In addition, the proportion of firms innovating has declined in recent years. According to the Innovation National Survey (2017-2018), the firm-innovation rate was 14.1%, below the 15.1% obtained in the round 2015-2016. Also, according to the Eighth National Survey on R&D Expenditure and Personnel, expenditure was $640,078 million, equivalent to 0.36% of GDP, compared to an OECD average of 2.34%.

Objetivos: 1) El PNPC fomenta la transformación continua y el aseguramiento de la pertinencia de los posgrados, para incrementar las capacidades científicas, humanísticas, tecnológicas y de innovación del país, que incorporen la generación y aplicación del conocimiento como un recurso para el desarrollo de la sociedad y la atención a los problemas, contribuyendo así a consolidar la transformación del país hacia el bienestar social, la sustentabilidad y el desarrollo cultural y económico. Iniciativa: Science in School Program (Programa Ciência na Escola) [PCE]. País: Brasil. Período: de 2019 a 2022. Relação com o tema: política de formação e carreira em CTI que não menciona mulheres nem gênero (temas: Competências STEM). A descrição não fala de mulheres nem de gênero. Atenção: esta iniciativa aparece só na edição 2023 do STIP Compass; o governo não a informou de novo em 2025, e ela pode ter sido encerrada ou substituída. Atenção: a fonte informa término em 2022. Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MCTI; Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação); Ministry of Economy (ME; Ministério da Economia). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): The Science in School Program (PCE) is a commitment to improving the teaching of science in education. Objetivos: 1) To improve science teaching in basic education schools. 2) To promote teaching through research aimed at solving problems. 3) To better qualify basic education teachers for science teaching. 4) To stimulate the interest of basic education students in scientific careers. 5) To identify young talents. 6) To encourage the implementation of innovative solutions that contribute to improving science teaching and learning. Público-alvo: Pesquisadores estabelecidos; Instituições de ensino superior; Estudantes do ensino médio. Temas no STIP: Competências STEM; Cultura de ciência, tecnologia e inovação. Instrumentos: Estratégias, agendas e planos (Decree); Campanhas de conscientização e divulgação; orçamento anual informado: de 5 a 20 milhões (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: sem avaliação informada. Contexto: In Brazil, the scientific teaching and learning process in basic education barely integrates educational institutions, be they universities, technological institutes or state and municipal basic education networks, as well as other institutions that deal with scientific production and dissemination (museums, fairs, olympics, etc). The Science in School Program was designed to fill this gap. By bringing university researchers closer to state and municipal education networks, the PCE aims to foster the development of methodologies aimed at integrating institutions, the induction of innovation and the interdisciplinary and collective solution of concrete problems of social reality.

Público-alvo: Mulheres; Grupos desfavorecidos e excluídos. Temas no STIP: Plano ou estratégia de CTI; Equidade, diversidade e inclusão (EDI). areas: mulheres e igualdade de gênero em ciência e tecnologia
detalhes: Fonte: EC-OECD STIP Compass (Comissão Europeia e OCDE), edição 2023 da pesquisa STIP (dados atualizados até dezembro de 2024); iniciativa 99993907, informada pelo governo da Argentina; última atualização no STIP: 06/02/2023. Iniciativa: National Program for Gender Equality in Science, Technology and Innovation (Programa Nacional de Igualdad de Géneros en Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación). País: Argentina. Período: desde 2020, sem data de término informada. Relação com o tema: iniciativa dedicada a mulheres ou à igualdade de gênero. Trecho sobre mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade: "National Program for an equal participation of women and the LGTBI + population at all levels and areas of the scientific-technological system." | "To make STI institutions conducive environments for women and people to LGTBI + perform and progress with equality and free from violence.". Atenção: esta iniciativa aparece só na edição 2023 do STIP Compass; o governo não a informou de novo em 2025, e ela pode ter sido encerrada ou substituída. Responsável: Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (MINCYT; Ministerio de Ciencia, Tecnología e Innovación). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): National Program for an equal participation of women and the LGTBI + population at all levels and areas of the scientific-technological system. Objetivos: 1) To make STI institutions conducive environments for women and people to LGTBI + perform and progress with equality and free from violence. 2) To integrate gender analysis into the content of policies, programs, and RDI projects from their design. 3) To promote equality for women and the LGTBI + population in access to hierarchical positions. 4) To articulate with different public and private organizations. 5) To cooperate in the development of studies, research and knowledge transfer with other organisms. Público-alvo: Mulheres. Temas no STIP: Equidade, diversidade e inclusão (EDI). Instrumentos: Serviços de informação e acesso a dados (Scientists (women) investigating COVID-19); orçamento anual informado: menos de 1 milhão (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: sem avaliação informada. Contexto: The Program arises within the framework of a State policy aimed at ensuring the conditions for that women and the LGTBI + community can develop in equality and in environments free of violence. (continuação) In turn, it is a response to debates within the system about participation and performance of women in the labor market and gender gaps in scientific careers and technological - debates that emerge from the diagnoses made in the past by the Ministry itself- and the articulation with the experiences of the Observatory of labor violence and genus (OVLG) of CONICET.

Iniciativa: Institutional Program of the National Council of Science and Technology (Programa Institucional del Consejo Nacional de Ciencia y Tecnología) [PI]. País: México. Período: de 2020 a 2024. Relação com o tema: política de CTI que inclui mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade entre seus objetivos ou públicos (o governo marcou Mulheres entre os grupos-alvo). Responsável: National Council for Humanities, Science and Technology (CONAHCYT; Consejo Nacional de Humanidades, Ciencias y Tecnologías). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): It defines the way in which the instruments of humanities, science, technology and innovation policy will be applied and operated in order to contribute to the fulfilment of the objectives, priorities, strategies and policies of the National Development Plan and the Special Programme for Science, Technology and Innovation. Objetivos: 1) 1: Strengthen the STI and other knowledge communities, through their formation, consolidation and linkage with different sectors of society, in order to address national priority problems with an inclusive approach to contribute to the general welfare of the population. 2) 2: Articulate an innovation ecosystem that integrates the different actors of scientific, technological and innovation development in the country to address national priorities, with strict care for the environment, respectful of the biocultural wealth and in favour of society. 3) 3: To increase the incidence of humanistic, scientific and technological knowledge in the solution of the country's priority problems, through the Strategic National Programmes and for the benefit of the population. 4) 4: Strengthen and consolidate the capacities of the country's scientific community to generate cutting-edge scientific knowledge with the potential to have an impact on the well-being of the population and care for the environment. 5) 5: Articulate and strengthen the country's scientific, humanistic and technological capacities by linking with regional actors to influence strategic national problems in favour of social benefit, environmental care, biocultural wealth and common goods.

detalhes: Fonte: EC-OECD STIP Compass (Comissão Europeia e OCDE), edição 2023 da pesquisa STIP (dados atualizados até dezembro de 2024); iniciativa 99994401, informada pelo governo do México; última atualização no STIP: 03/06/2023. Iniciativa: Programme for the Incorporation of Students with Disabilities Into National Postgraduate Courses (Programa para la Incorporación de Estudiantes con Discapacidad a Posgrados Nacionales). País: México. Período: desde 2013, sem data de término informada. Relação com o tema: política de CTI que inclui mulheres, gênero ou parentalidade entre seus objetivos ou públicos (o governo marcou o tema Equidade, diversidade e inclusão). Atenção: esta iniciativa aparece só na edição 2023 do STIP Compass; o governo não a informou de novo em 2025, e ela pode ter sido encerrada ou substituída. Responsável: National Council for Humanities, Science and Technology (CONAHCYT; Consejo Nacional de Humanidades, Ciencias y Tecnologías). Descrição (texto informado pelo governo): Strengthen the academic skills of people with disabilities through specific scholarships that enable them to enter postgraduate programmes and contribute to reducing the disadvantages caused by marginalisation, educational inequality and discrimination. Objetivos: 1) To contribute to the entry of people with disabilities to master's studies by strengthening their academic skills, promoting equal access to third level studies and training professionals who contribute to local, regional and national development. Público-alvo: Estudantes de graduação e mestrado. Temas no STIP: Equidade, diversidade e inclusão (EDI). Instrumentos: Bolsas de estudo, de pesquisa e de pós-graduação; orçamento anual informado: não se aplica (o arquivo do STIP não informa a moeda); avaliação: sem avaliação informada. Contexto: In accordance with the National Development Plan 2019-2024, affirmative actions are implemented to provide support focused on historically excluded population groups. Between 1 September 2020 and 30 June 2021, a total of 3,571 scholarships were administered to support specific populations to promote social inclusion, of which 22.7% (812) went to students from indigenous populations to pursue postgraduate studies, 77.1% (2,754) to Mexican mothers who are heads of household to pursue full-time, school-based professional studies, and 0.2% (5) to incorporate students with disabilities to pursue postgraduate studies. (continuação) Of these, 19.9% had motor disabilities, 64.5% had sensory disabilities (hearing, visual, language and communication), 9.1% had multiple disabilities and 6.5% had mental disabilities.

nome: Debate de política de CTI 2025: Recursos humanos em CTI na Argentina (OECD STIP Compass)
categoria: Debate de Política / OECD STIP Compass
tipo: Debate nacional de política de CTI (OECD STIP Compass)
areas: Recursos humanos em CTI
detalhes: Fonte: EC-OECD STIP Compass, Policy Debates 2025 (texto informado pelo governo da Argentina, atualizado em 10/04/2025). Debate de política de CTI: Recursos humanos em CTI (STI human resources debates). País: Argentina. The ongoing debate is centered on the structure and criteria of career paths for researchers and technologists. Recent policy proposals have sought to broaden the scope of technology transfer careers, enhance public-private internships, and revise evaluation criteria to better reflect the diverse contributions of individuals in these fields. In this context, discussions also consider the need to strengthen merit-based selection and progression mechanisms, as well as to prioritise strategic areas aligned with national development goals. These initiatives are essential as they aim to create more dynamic career pathways in science, technology, and innovation. By updating the evaluation criteria, we can ensure that a wider array of contributions are recognised, including activities related to innovation, technology development, collaboration with industry, and the adoption of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, thereby fostering a more diverse and innovative research environment. Additionally, promoting public-private internships can bridge the gap between theoretical knowledge and practical application, enhancing the skill sets of researchers and technologists, and contribute to improving the employability and mobility of highly skilled human resources across sectors. The expansion of technology transfer careers is also a significant step. It opens up opportunities for professionals to engage directly with the market and society, applying their expertise to real-world challenges and enhancing the impact of scientific research on societal advancement. At the same time, there is an ongoing discussion on how to optimize the allocation of public resources for human capital development, including a shift towards more targeted and impactful funding schemes that prioritise excellence and critical mass over fragmentation. This is complemented by efforts to strengthen linkages between academia, public research organisations, and the productive sector, as well as to promote more flexible career trajectories, including temporary mobility between public and private institutions.

Trecho sobre mulheres ou gênero: "The Government's strategy centers on mission-driven STKI as a core element of public action, aimed at an economic model that protects ecosystems, reduces structural, gender and territorial inequalities, and builds technological sovereignty." | "In this context, MinCiencia has increased its contributions to the Just Socio-Ecological Transition Agenda and the Gender Equality Agenda, ensuring that policy decisions align with public values and intergenerational justice.". In alignment with the new development model promoted by the Chilean Government, which focuses on productive diversification, socio-ecological sustainability, and effective decentralization of growth, there is a consolidated effort to strengthen public investment in Science, Technology, Knowledge, and Innovation (STKI). This effort is recognised as a strategic pillar for the country's productive transformation. The recent establishment of the Productivity and Development Fund, financed through revenues from lithium exploitation, marks a significant step towards creating a higher economic value with territorial justice. However, structural challenges remain, particularly the need for a sustained increase in the gross domestic expenditure on research and development (GERD) as a percentage of GDP (0.39% to the year 2022). This persistent gap limits Chile's capacity to address ongoing global transitions. The Ministry of Science, Technology, Knowledge, and Innovation (MinCiencia) acknowledges the development of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, quantum computing, and biotechnologies. These technologies not only offer an opportunity to enhance national productivity but are also crucial in tackling significant challenges like the climate emergency, disaster resilience, and improving the quality of life. Addressing these issues requires a policy approach that integrates technological infrastructure, enabling regulatory frameworks, and the training of human capital, focusing on rights, equity, and territorial relevance. The Government's strategy centers on mission-driven STKI as a core element of public action, aimed at an economic model that protects ecosystems, reduces structural, gender and territorial inequalities, and builds technological sovereignty.

A key component of this strategy is the promotion of Science-and Technology-Based Enterprises (STBEs). These enterprises not only generate quality employment and positive externalities in their environments but also act as concrete vehicles for transferring knowledge to strategic productive sectors. Their development is led by the National Agency for Research and Development (ANID) and supported through programmes aimed at accelerating their creation, consolidation, and expansion, with a focus on relevant technological solutions to national challenges. Similarly, the role of accredited public and private universities as hubs for scientific, technological, and territorial innovation is fundamental for a just and sustainable productive transformation. The State is reinforcing its commitment to these institutions through policies that seek to consolidate capacities in Research, Development, Innovation, and Entrepreneurship (R&D&I&E), with particular emphasis on those that respond to local needs, diversify the national productive matrix, and promote high-impact entrepreneurship. This renewed momentum for STKI is embedded in a national vision that places the economy at the service of people and territories. It recognises knowledge not as a luxury, but as an essential tool to build a more just, inclusive, and sustainable future for Chile. In addition to the national STI policy, Chile is developing other strategic policies. These include the artificial intelligence (AI) strategy, the CTCI gender policy, the green hydrogen strategy, and a roadmap for transitioning to a circular economy. These policies collectively aim to guide the country's scientific advancements comprehensively.

This issue is currently being discussed in the Chilean Congress. Other ongoing debate questions are whether the overall research expenditures in the country are sufficiently funded. The government primarily funds individual projects, which often lack provisions for the long-term support of critical research infrastructure, such as university laboratories and administrative operations. Furthermore, the Better Work in Research Agenda is an initiative that seeks to monitor research careers or trajectories and the conditions surrounding them, complementing the efforts to fund research infrastructure adequately. Additionally, legislative attention is directed towards a Technology Transfer Bill and an Artificial Intelligence Bill, both under review by the National Congress. These bills are crucial as they will further define the legal and operational framework for technology transfer and AI development in Chile and stimulate the creation and development of science and technology-based companies (“EBCT”) from higher education institutions.

categoria: Debate de Política / OECD STIP Compass

detalhes: Fonte: EC-OECD STIP Compass, Policy Debates 2025 (texto informado pelo governo do Chile, atualizado em 27/03/2025). Debate de política de CTI: Recursos humanos em CTI (STI human resources debates). País: Chile. In Chile, current policy debates on government support for human resources for research and innovation (R&D&I) are increasingly focusing on the need to transition from a model centred almost exclusively on academic training to a more comprehensive approach. This new model aims to promote effective insertion, intersectoral mobility, and the development of career paths within the science, technology, knowledge, and innovation (STKI) system. One of the primary concerns is the limited articulation between the growing volume of advanced human capital, which is mainly formed through national and international scholarships, and the actual employment opportunities available in the public, private, and productive sectors. This mismatch has drawn criticism from academic communities as well as researcher unions and associations, which are advocating for a review of the sustainability of the current system. A second focal point of the debate centers on the need to redefine the instruments that support labour market insertion, particularly in the private sector and intermediate institutions such as technology centres, NGOs, and regional governments. These areas face structural barriers including low demand for R&D, a lack of differentiated tax incentives, and a weak regional institutional framework for absorbing scientific-technological talent. In response, proposals are being put forward that suggest more flexible insertion programmes, new training schemes oriented towards innovation and entrepreneurship, and enhanced capacity building in R&D management and technology transfer. Furthermore, there is active discussion on the need to revise the criteria for evaluating academic and scientific performance. The proposed revisions include incorporating dimensions such as engagement with the environment, participation in social innovation, and intersectoral collaboration. These debates indicate a paradigm shift towards a more inclusive and flexible human resources policy in ICTC, which is oriented towards maximising the economic and social impact of knowledge.

The ongoing debates in the governance of science, technology, and innovation (STI) policies are centred on ensuring that strategic direction is aligned with public interest, social justice, and territorial action. There is a growing consensus on the need to transition away from centralized and technocratic models towards frameworks that promote representative and equal participation, free from conflicts of interest. Furthermore, there is a call for the inclusion of differential, gender, and territorial approaches in policy-making. This is crucial for addressing the diverse needs and challenges across different regions and communities. The coordination between national and local levels, exemplified by initiatives such as the Departmental Council for Science, Technology and Innovation (CODECTI, which serves as the space for coordination and consultation of STI policy in each department of the country), is essential for effective governance. Additionally, there is a push to broaden the social base of the national system of science, technology and innovation (SNCTeI) by acknowledging the contributions of non-academic actors and embracing diverse forms of knowledge. These discussions highlight the importance of evolving governance models to be more inclusive and representative of a wider array of stakeholders and perspectives.

Debate de política de CTI: Inovação empresarial (Business innovation policy debates). País: Colômbia. Trecho sobre mulheres ou gênero: "Another important area of debate concerns the need for differentiated public policies to reduce gender gaps, foster female and minority entrepreneurship, and strengthen the popular economy.". The main debates currently revolve around sustainable financing, effective regulation, and the need for a territorial approach that connects the five development helices: the State, academia, the business sector, civil society, and the environment. In Colombia and the region, the private sector benefits significantly from subsidies without adequately investing in strategic areas such as technology. In response to this situation, the Mission-Oriented Public Policy (PIIOM) has been adopted, through which the State directs public financing toward achieving strategic objectives such as clean energy and the bioeconomy. At the same time, there is an ongoing discussion about bureaucratic barriers and the accessibility of government programs and resources that aim to foster business innovation and entrepreneurship. Many entrepreneurs highlight the difficulties they face in accessing incentives, the lack of coordination among public entities, and the need to simplify administrative procedures. They also call for ensuring a more agile and effective implementation of programs and projects that stimulate innovation. Access to financing is one of the most debated topics, focusing on the effectiveness of state financial instruments and the urgent need to create mechanisms to provide seed capital. Another important area of debate concerns the need for differentiated public policies to reduce gender gaps, foster female and minority entrepreneurship, and strengthen the popular economy. Additionally, concerns are raised about the effectiveness of coordination among national systems related to science, technology, innovation, education, foreign trade, and even international cooperation. Persistent criticism points to fragmentation, the lack of a long-term vision, weak inter-institutional coordination, and the limited impact of dispersed policies—all of which hinder sustained progress in innovation.

Debate de política de CTI: Recursos humanos em CTI (STI human resources debates). País: Costa Rica. In Costa Rica, policy discussions on human resources for research and innovation are increasingly focused on strengthening the national talent pipeline, particularly in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) fields. While the number of researchers per capita and PhD graduates in priority areas faced challenges (398 per million inhabitants), stakeholders across academia, government, and industry are actively promoting initiatives to expand advanced training programs, foster international mobility, and align educational pathways with emerging technological demands. Current efforts aim to improve incentives for talent retention, support reintegration of researchers trained abroad, and encourage interdisciplinary and applied research careers. These actions are being framed within broader strategies such as the National STI Policy and the National AI Strategy, reflecting a shared commitment to developing a robust and future-ready research and innovation workforce. Another key focus of current policy discussions is strengthening the integration of researchers into the private sector and expanding stable, long-term career pathways in public research institutions. Stakeholders are advancing proposals for public-private research fellowships, as well as reforms in recruitment and career progression mechanisms to foster interdisciplinary and applied research. In parallel, efforts are underway to align postgraduate scholarship programs with strategic national priorities—including artificial intelligence, bioeconomy, and clean technologies—ensuring that talent development responds to the evolving demands of the innovation ecosystem. There is also growing momentum to promote innovation-oriented skills among students and professionals through short-term training, mentorships, and stronger academia-industry collaboration, building a more agile and responsive STI workforce. Although some of these ideas are incorporated in recent strategies like the PNCTI and the National AI Strategy, significant policy shifts are still necessary.

detalhes: Fonte: EC-OECD STIP Compass, Policy Debates 2025 (texto informado pelo governo do México, atualizado em 14/02/2025). Debate de política de CTI: Governança da CTI (Governance debates). País: México. Trecho sobre mulheres ou gênero: "Its goals include strengthening Mexico's capabilities and reducing its technological dependence by training and consolidating the scientific, technological, humanities, and research community with a focus on gender parity.". On November 28, 2024, the Organic Law of the Federal Public Administration was amended, creating the Secretariat of Science, Humanities, Technology, and Innovation, which is set to commence operations on January 1, 2025. The primary objective of the Secretariat is to ensure that every individual has the right to enjoy the benefits of scientific development, humanistic progress, and technological innovation. The new policy framework in Mexico aims to transform the nation into a sovereign scientific and technological power. This transformation is envisioned through the promotion of collaborative research, technological development, and innovation in strategic sectors, ultimately fostering development that leads to shared well-being and prosperity. Currently, the integration of the Science, Humanities, Technology, and Innovation Sectoral Programme is in progress. Its goals include strengthening Mexico's capabilities and reducing its technological dependence by training and consolidating the scientific, technological, humanities, and research community with a focus on gender parity. The programme also promotes technological development by maturing and scaling technologies that align with regional and national priorities, thereby contributing to social well-being. It aims to generate knowledge through basic and interdisciplinary research and to strengthen the infrastructure necessary to tackle priority issues. Additionally, it seeks to implement mechanisms for linkage, modernisation, and technology transfer and innovation between the academic, productive, public, and social sectors. These efforts are aligned with national priorities and are oriented towards social well-being through inter-institutional collaboration networks that carry out strategic projects, promote the transfer of knowledge and innovation, and address local, national, and international challenges. The transition from the National Council for Humanities, Sciences, and Technologies to a Secretariat involved the regulatory harmonisation of many activities governing the sector.

categoria: Debate de Política / OECD STIP Compass
tipo: Debate nacional de política de CTI (OECD STIP Compass)

Debate de política de CTI: Recursos humanos em CTI (STI human resources debates). País: México. Mexico has recently undergone significant changes, and the scientific sector is no exception. The reform of Article 3 of the Constitution in 2019 led to the creation of the new Law on Humanities, Sciences, Technologies, and Innovation. This law recognises that every individual has the right to enjoy the benefits of scientific and technological innovation and mandates the State to provide sufficient resources and incentives. It also guarantees free access to public postgraduate programmes recognised within the National Postgraduate System. The political debate surrounding government support for human resources in research and innovation acknowledges the budgetary constraints that must be addressed to ensure this constitutional right for everyone, irrespective of their socioeconomic or cultural conditions. There are two major debates in this area. The first concerns the training of the scientific and humanities community, specifically whether funding private higher education institutions and research centres imposes a budgetary burden that distorts plural and equitable access to science at the expense of collective benefit. A similar discussion arises around the equitable distribution for postgraduate studies abroad versus prioritising support within the national system. The second debate focuses on strengthening the scientific community, including the prioritisation of support for researchers in the public sector versus those in the private or foreign sectors. This debate extends to how the community sustains itself, questioning whether support mechanisms should prioritise productivity or career development, while respecting diversity of thought and socioeconomic and cultural backgrounds. Additionally, there is a discussion on whether scientific activity should address public problems. Given the existing disparities across different regions of the country, the scientific community experiences inequalities that prompt a broader dialogue on these issues.

These forums presented a diverse range of topics, with significant emphasis on coordination, water, energy, strengthening of universities and schools, teacher support, health, gender and inclusion policies, and scientific dissemination. By 2025, the budget programs of Branch 38, which focuses on Science, Humanities, Technology, and Innovation, were aligned with seven of the 17 SDGs outlined in the UN 2030 Agenda.

Peru has made significant strides in enhancing the capacities, skills, and competencies of its human capital in the fields of science, technology, and innovation. The country is actively promoting doctoral programs through inter-institutional alliances and increasing funding for scholarships and internships. Currently, internships are in both academia and industry, with a higher proportion in academia because in Peru, unfortunately, we have not made progress in implementing incentives for the incorporation of researchers in technology companies. Additionally, incentives are being provided to improve the retention and attraction of talent, thereby increasing dedication to STI activities. Training for technological managers in science, technology, and innovation is also being emphasized as part of these policy initiatives. Furthermore, Peru is committed to promoting the continued participation of women, girls, and adolescents in scientific research, technological development, and innovation activities. This is being achieved through strategic alliances with educational institutions, research centers, and international organizations that support gender equity in the scientific and technological fields. These efforts are part of a broader strategy to build a robust framework for research and innovation, ensuring that Peru remains competitive and innovative in the global STI landscape.

To achieve this goal, a series of strategies have been developed. These include the National Science Fair, Peru with Science, departmental forums on science, technology, and innovation, and the creation of Science and Technology Clubs. In response to the rapid advancement of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, Peru has adopted an approach focused on the ethical, inclusive, and responsible use of these tools.
